records.region: Northwestern Alaska; Wulik River and Kivalina Lagoon corridor
records.geographic_disambiguation: Wulik River as the receiving-river identity of the selected connected system, including an unnamed eastern mountain feeder and the lower delta-channel approach to Kivalina Lagoon.
records.completion_scope: Three original USGSTopo views and bounded overlapping reading crops were visually inspected. They establish ordinary corridor correspondence for the one selected mainstem fragment and all 35 stored parts: eastern feeder opening, receiving Wulik join, upper valley, West Fork and Ikalukrok junction settings, lower braided channel, wetland/delta passage and actual terminal in the Kivalina Lagoon entry setting. Generalized bends and local line offsets stay within the depicted connected corridors and do not create a missing selected through-link.
records.supported_name_scope: Repeated Wulik River labels directly identify the selected receiving trunk, middle braided valley and lower delta. The eastern opening feeder remains unnamed in the read cartography; the Wulik identity is representative rather than a scalar assignment to that feeder or the lagoon.

scope_limits: The eastern feeder has no established name in the read cartography; candidate_name for that component remains null.
Wulik River is a representative connected-system identity, not a formal assertion that every selected feeder or lagoon carries that name.
The selected line simplifies bends and is locally offset from detailed mapped channels. Exact source, name-change, bank, confluence and endpoint vertices are not assigned.
The actual terminal is bounded to the Wulik delta and Kivalina Lagoon entry setting; no selected open-ocean extension is inferred.
Map reading does not establish present flow, tidal stage, water level, engineering operation or formal registry status.

records.region: Whiting Lake–South Whiting–Whiting corridor, northwestern British Columbia and southeastern Alaska
records.material_pending_reason: The selected southern opening, westward and northward bend, and lake approach in FID9018 parts1–14 lack an established through-link into the first depicted southern arm of Whiting Lake. Lake passage and the South Whiting–Whiting receiving corridor are supported.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The receiving-system candidate is supported for the lake-outlet, South Whiting and Whiting corridor only. It is not a completed whole-system identification because the selected southern opening-to-lake interval remains unestablished.
records.completion_scope: All64 parts of both selected mainstem fragments have been considered. FID9018 parts1–14 retain a material opening-and-lake-approach gap. The remaining lake passage, outlet, river junction, cross-border reach, Alaska valley and actual selected terminal have ordinary source correspondence. One material-pending primary status is used; this is not a completed representative identity or completed naming-scope hold.
records.supported_name_scope: The receiving-system candidate is supported for the lake-outlet, South Whiting and Whiting corridor only. It is not a completed whole-system identification because the selected southern opening-to-lake interval remains unestablished.

scope_limits: The selected southern opening has not been assigned to any particular named glacier, stream or subglacial flow path.
Cartographic lake and river names are component-specific; the lake, South Whiting and Whiting labels are not interchangeable.
Historical field descriptions are used only for the observations actually read, without asserting present channel conditions or using unseen pocket maps.
Composite federal cartography does not establish current ice limits, lake levels, precise banks, flow states or a formal naming-registry decision.

records.region: Northeastern Manitoba, east of the Hudson Bay Railway and through Wapusk National Park to Hudson Bay.
records.candidate_name_role: Broad River is the named shared downstream trunk and coastal outlet; Hoot Creek is the distinct selected headward feeder. Parks Canada prints Anaskosipiy beside Broad River.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Three overlapping original maps support the chosen western lake-chain opening, the Hoot Creek feeder, its connection to Broad River, the complete selected Broad trunk and the actual Hudson Bay outlet. Broad River is supported as a representative system identity; the separately named Hoot Creek and unnamed headward lakes retain their own scope.
records.completion_scope: All 13 selected parts, chosen opening, small-lake/channel connections, intermediate joins and actual terminal at ordinary corridor scale. No exact-bank, current-flow, operating-state or endpoint-precision requirement.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative downstream river and connected Hoot Creek–Broad River system identity; not one uniform name for the selected headward lakes, feeder and every reach.

scope_limits: The headward small lakes are not assigned names from neighboring lake labels. The chosen opening is a model-selected location, not an assertion about Broad River’s natural source.
The selected Hoot Creek feeder differs from the separately drawn southwestern Broad River branch. Representative system identity does not require replacing either reach name.
Parks Canada supplies the Cree label Anaskosipiy; orthographic variants or registry status were not independently established.

The originals depict the lowland lake/stream and coastal tidal-flat corridor without a selected reservoir, glacier or managed diversion. No modern hydraulic, seasonal-flow or operating-state determination is made.
Historical/generalized cartography supports ordinary corridor correspondence, not current shorelines, precise banks or exact mouth vertices.
Incidental excluded naming-record search results were not opened or used. Search excerpts and supplied geometry were not treated as substantive original-map evidence.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
